reason: The cited evidence supports the formation of TiC in W-based systems via SPS and its benefits for heat flux resistance, irradiation resistance, and grain boundary stabilization in W alloys. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to W–Cu composites, where the role of TiC at W–Cu interfaces and its effect on thermal conductivity are not addressed by the cited passages.
premises: TiC can be formed in-situ during spark plasma sintering of W-based powder mixtures containing Ti and C.
TiC dispersions in W-based materials can withstand very high heat fluxes (up to 200 MW/m2).
TiC dispersions in W-based materials increase irradiation resistance and recrystallization temperature.
TiC dispersions in W-based materials provide grain boundary strengthening and resist grain boundary migration at elevated temperatures.
